_what_this_is: The nine cases in cases.json, each posted alone into a room by a human and pushed through the shipped gate: stage 0's rules (gate.ts), then stage 1's cut (watch.ts at the shipped 0.600 over llama.ts's reading against a real llama-server). One row per case, saying where the case stopped and what the model read if it was asked.
_why_this_file_exists: The work table beside this file counts what a work model does with the nine cases, and that count is only a cost where the cases actually arrive. The work model is stage 2: a message reaches it when stage 0 fast-passes it or when stage 1 reads act, and is consumed with nothing spent otherwise. Without this reading, 'spoke when it should not 3/3' has no price and 'delivered 6/6' has no ceiling.

rig.flags: -m <model.gguf> --alias <name> --host 127.0.0.1 --port <port> -c 4096 -np 1 -ngl 99, plus --mmproj for the model that carries a projector
rig.transport: the kernel's own, not a paraphrase: classify() from src/gate.ts decides each entry, watchAs() from src/watch.ts owns the cut, llamaWatchModel() from src/llama.ts does the forward pass and readingOf()'s summing, and the mask is bindOverServer() over skeletonOf(watch-v1) — the same ids the runtime measures
rig.not_re_implemented: no threshold, no strip rule and no probability arithmetic appears in the driver: it wraps the kernel's model only to keep the number the kernel read
rig.judgements: one message per world, drained alone, so no case rides on another's delta and each reading belongs to the text it is recorded against
rig.sender: a human, in an unmuted group room; the bot is named Echo and the room watches a nightly batch, because two cases name the bot and a mention is what makes stage 0 fast-pass them
rig.determinism: two full runs, both recorded; every row identical to four decimal places, counts identical. A probability read has no sampling, so this confirms the rig rather than a setting

cases.note: the same nine the work table was measured on, read from that file rather than repeated here — a second copy of a case set is a second thing to drift

what_was_not_measured: Batching. Each case was judged alone with window 10. The runtime judges a room's delta — a summary plus several entries — and a different box is a different prompt, so a case that reads 0.2935 here may read otherwise beside two others. This is a controlled reading of the cases, not a replay of a live room.

Any watch model but the shipped one. Stage 1 runs LFM2.5-VL-3B, so these figures do not move with the work-model choice — they bound it. A different watch model is a different gate and needs its own reading.

Any cut but 0.600. The three refused should-speak cases read 0.1995, 0.2935 and 0.362, so no cut above 0.363 keeps them out and none below 0.199 would; a cut between changes which of them arrive. Moving it is the host's word, not this file's.

Why stage 1 refuses them. Two of the three refused should-speak cases are Chinese, which agrees with the recorded calibration's weak side (calibration/provenance.md: in Chinese, no cut exceeds 8/12) — but that is agreement, not a cause, and nothing here isolates it.
Whether the accepted case is answered well. Reaching the work model is the whole claim; what the work model then does with it is the table in measured.json.
